title: Execution sandbox hardening + documentation (CI: no-net/RO-FS/limits/non-root; learner: WASM isolation, caps, graceful timeout)
context: open-coding-curriculum is an open CC-BY (prose) / MIT (code) curriculum of beginner programming lessons with graded, runnable exercises across languages. Every exercise carries a reference solution proven correct in CI (solutionVerified:true), learner code runs zero-install in-browser via WASM, and all content is machine-readable structured data so third parties can build on it. The project targets absolute beginners — self-learners, public-library patrons, under-resourced school students, career-changers — and operates under a donated-compute lane with no server-side execution of learner code and no partner confirmed yet (verifiedNeed:false). The security model depends entirely on the two execution environments being provably safe: the CI correctness backend must not allow a reference solution to reach the network or exceed resource limits, and the in-browser WASM runner must not allow a learner's exercise to hang or abuse their browser. Hardening and documenting both is a M3 exit gate.
objective: Harden and document both execution sandboxes: (1) the CI correctness backend — no network, read-only FS, CPU/memory/wall-clock caps, non-root; (2) the in-browser WASM runner — WASM isolation, resource caps, graceful timeout on runaway code.
acceptanceCriteria: CI correctness backend is verified to run with no network access (outbound blocked), read-only filesystem, CPU and memory caps, wall-clock time limit, and non-root user.
A reference solution attempting network access is demonstrated to fail the CI gate.
A reference solution exceeding resource limits is demonstrated to fail the CI gate.
In-browser WASM runner enforces resource caps: CPU time limit terminates runaway JS/Python without hanging the learner's browser tab.
Graceful timeout message is shown to the learner when a timeout occurs; no silent hang.
Both sandboxes are documented in a security/sandbox doc committed to the repository: constraints, how they are enforced, and how to verify them.
pnpm build && pnpm test && pnpm lint pass.
output: A merged PR with hardened sandbox configurations for both execution environments and a committed sandbox security documentation document.
